title: Reasons 1-3: order of the universe; supreme unity/truth/goodness; if many, absurdities
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): YE FIRST from ye order belonging toward ye universe's parts — where order is, something one unto which ye rest are reduced must be. Aristotle: plurality of rulerships not good, one ruler. Athanasius: multitude of gods is nullity of gods. YE SECOND: God is highest unity, truth, goodness — cannot be except unique plus pure. YE THIRD: if many gods, either differ altogether or are one or partly both — first absurd; if second, already not many but one.
pass_b_english: THE FIRST is taken from the order of the universe's parts. Where there is order, there must be something one to which the rest are reduced. Aristotle: a plurality of rulerships is not good; let there be one ruler. Athanasius: a multitude of gods is a nullity of gods.
THE SECOND: God is highest unity, highest truth, highest goodness, which cannot be except unique and pure.
THE THIRD: if there were many gods, they either differ altogether, or are altogether one, or partly both: the first is absurd; if the second, they were already not many but one.
source_text: PRIMA sumitur ab ordine partium universi. Ubi ordo est, unum esse aliquid oportet ad quod cetera reducantur. Aristoteles: Non est bonum pluralitas principatuum: unus princeps esto. Athanasius: Multitudo deorum nullitas est deorum. SECUNDA: Deus summa est unitas, summa veritas, summa bonitas, quae non potest esse nisi unica & pura. TERTIA: si plures dii sint, aut omnino differunt, aut omnino unum sunt, aut partim differunt partim unum: primum absurdum; si alterum, jam non plures sed unus.
